The police force is WAY understaffed and crime is terrible and feels like its getting worse.  You can't expect police to help fight crime when there are only a few working at a time (working extra to fill in the gaps) and jumping from report call to report call.  No wonder you can't keep cops...they are burned out!  Used to be nice to have actual Olathe police dispatchers as well
I also think the public schools have gone down hill over the past 20 years we've lived in Olathe.  I had an instance over Covid where my 7th grader was sent WALKING home for an "exposure" without even making contact with either of us parents OR anyone listed on paperwork as being an emergency contact!  She came home at 10 am so had she not made it home we wouldn't have known she was missing until well after 3pm!  We are lucky she didnt get snatched and human trafficked!  All I got from the school was hung up on and treated as if I was ridiculous!  I am not impressed by Olathe schools at all!  The schools should have never been shut down and all that accomplished was giving me 3 teens with debilitating social anxiety!  They won't even go to a drive thru because they will have to talk to someone!  The whole thing is shameful!  Wish we would have leaders with a backbone who would have stood up to the nonsense including the school board and teachers unions!  Schools exist to teach the basics (Math, reading, science etc.)  Not indoctrination into woke ideology.

1. I don't know ANYONE who likes the taste of their city water, NO MATTER WHAT CITY THEY LIVE IN!!!  That's why sales of filters and bottled water is a billion dollar industry!  So, it's not in indictment on Olathe, it's just the way it is!

2. Government is NEVER EFFICIENT because ...

     a. Your don't compete with anyone
     b. It's not your money
     c. Your inefficiencies can be ignored by simply redistributing taxes or worse, raising taxes

          So, you cannot name a city service that I truly believe is a bargain!  Even though it's off topic, the closest I come to loving any city service offered here in Olathe is your bulk item pickup.  It's not the bargain that it once was, but it's still WAY BETTER THAN private industry's costs!
column131:
1. When I moved to Olathe, I was SHOCKED to learn that yard waste MUST BE put in those evil paper bags!  

     a. When I lived in NC, I used to use 33 gallon plastic trash cans (with lids) to dispose of pine needles.  They are light weight, work well, AND are one-time sunk costs versus CONSTANTLY buying more of those yard bags, which ... by the way, come from trees!
     b. It's very typical of big government that LOVES to dictate!

2. When I moved here, you had to "opt in" to Olathe's recycle program (at a cost).  I decided not to.  Within a few months, the fascist City of Olathe simply dropped off recycle containers to everyone and said in effect, "You're going to pay whether or not you participate in the recycle program or not."  

    I love how politicians call themselves, "public servants," but funny how they just push us around, isn't it?  Or put another way: WHOM ARE YOU SERVING when you decide for me that I get a recycle bin, no matter what and ... bonus, I get to pay for it whether I want it or not?

3. Just recently my son, who lets his trash stack up in his room, brought down 6 to 8 garbage bags of trash, which was too many to fit in the trash bin.  So, I just put them by the curb, FOOLISHLY THINKING ... they will pick them up.  NOPE!  They just left them.

    Note: Those bags were each about 80 percent water bottles and each weighed just a couple of pounds.  So, it wasn't about the size or the weight.  It's just about government reminding us again and again that we the people submit to you and your almighty rules.  

4. As I said in a previous response, government CANNOT be efficient, because it has no competition, it has a seemingly endless supply of money to grab at will, and government doesn't care, because it's almighty!  

    So, again, it's a joke that you invite me to lie about how happy I am with the costs of your city services.  You just raised my home tax appraisal by 30-plus percent!  You all just do what ever the hell you want to do and we're supposed to gush over your performance?  No thank you!
column146:
I've NEVER heard of ANY recycling program that is profitable!  Just as I mentioned above, you imposed your recycle bins on EVERYONE!  It's a silly woke "service" that is designed NOT to do anything meaningful (certainly not in a cost-efficient manner!), but instead to make the environmental wackos feel all warm and gooey inside because we together are saving "Mother Earth."

But in the meantime, undoubtedly your recycle program is spewing tax dollars with ... once again, gross inefficiencies and ZERO chance of ever turning it into a profitable effort.

The city seems focused too much on "progress" at the expensive of nature, family and community.  The rezoning of R1 land to to R3 and R4 multi-tenant apartment complexes disrupts established neighborhoods, increases traffic, increase crime and is often executed for out-of-state business interests.  There are fewer single-family homes due to the excessive focus on apartment complexes.  Please stop allowing out-of-state business interests to raze our natural timbers and pastures to the ground simply to erect cheaply built, mono design apartment complexes.  The Olathe City Council is a disgrace and I suspect many members are on the take, accepting bribes or gifts for voting to approve certain concessions. 

Divergent diamond interchanges are proving to be an eyesore as they host upwards 30 signs just to "explain" the traffic flow to commuters.  It also requires the destruction of all median green space and has not produced an improvement in traffic flow.  It seems I sit in my car, idling away, every time I approach the DDI at K10/Ridgeview and 119th/I-35.  Every single time.  When standard intersections existed, I got through without stopping approximately 50% of the time.  Please STOP building divergent diamond interchanges and roundabouts. 

The destruction of timber land and green space to run 119th street through to Woodland is a disgrace.  Simply improve the existing corridors at 135th, College and K-10.  Stop destroying green space, please!

The installation of LED lighting has been an absolute bust.  On the main thoroughfares, where LED lighting has a place, we're frequently blinded with violet/ultra-violet light from the failed LED lamp heads.  The City went cheap, buying crap Chinese-made LED lamps, and now we're all paying the price.  Invest in American made street lighting.  LED lamps in neighborhoods is just bad idea.  High pressure sodium lamps cast a warm glow that is very inviting and lacks disruptive blue light that has negatively impacted our nocturnal wildlife.  The argument of a "superior CRI" is moot in neighborhoods with little to no crime.  Please, get rid of the ultra-white LED headlamps that bring a clinical or prison yard look to our neighborhood streets.  Bring back either HPS lamps or lower color temp LED for neighborhoods.  A gentle and warm 2700K street lamp looks so much better than the 3500K+ lamps the city has been installing.  2700K LED would achieve the goal of reducing energy consumption (LED) while also eliminating much of the blue light of the current bright white lamps (moving to 2700K).  This would benefit nocturnal wildlife and restore the warm, inviting ambiance the City stole when they swith to ultra white LED lamps.  

Stop implementing change for the the sake of change.  Some things simply work as-is and new isn't always better.  Fix the real problems and don't be too proud to admit when you're wrong.  LED lamps greater than 2700K in neighborhoods was a poor decision.  Roll it back.  Divergent diamond interchanges are ugly, increase idling emissions, and simply don't work as the computer models suggest.  Get rid of them.  Rezone R1 land adjacent to established neighborhoods runs counter to the original plans for beautiful Olathe.  Stop catering to out-of-state business interests and start respecting establish Olathe citizens and development plans.  The property taxes in Olathe are ridiculous. Stop spending so much and lower our taxes.  Spend money on streets, utilities and parks.  Stop spending money on entitlement programs and other pork that isn't related to our core infrastructure and utilities.
